title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells - Nature Energy
text:
AbstractSolution processing has great advantages in lowering the cost for fabricating chalcopyrite solar cells, yet challenges remain in controlling the crystallization process and achieving desirable composition. Here we show a precursor linkage strategy to achieve uniform Cu(In,Ga)Se2 chalcopyrite thin films using simple metal salts and thiourea (Tu) as precursors. By introducing an acetate anion (OAc−) with both hydrogen- and coordination-bonding capabilities, a molecular network connecting Cu–Tu and In– or Ga– complexes can be established in the precursor solution, which facilitates controlled reactions and prevents the formation of undesired secondary phases during crystallization. The coordination between Ga and OAc− also enables uniform and complete Ga alloying for high-purity single-phase Cu(In,Ga)Se2 films. The resulting solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 18.53% (certified 17.53%). Our work shows that phase-pure multi-element chalcogenide materials can be achieved by rational and precise design of solution chemistry.
